name: Blood Shards of Agamaggan

summary: Across the Barrens, the Blood Shards of Agamaggan still hold the power of a fallen boar god. Quilboar say his blood sank into the earth and hardened into red stones. At Camp Taurajo, captive Mangletooth trades that power to the Horde for his own reasons.

sections.title: The Boar God's Legacy
sections.body:
Quilboar lore tells how Agamaggan fell ten thousand years ago in the War of the Ancients. His blood raised giant thorn mazes across the plains, then sank into the soil and seeped into minerals. In time, it hardened into blood-red stones.

The quilboar honor the shards as sacred remnants of their creator. They gather them from mineral seams and holy grounds, then use them as totems in battle and sorcery.

sections.title: Spite from a Wooden Cage
sections.body:
The tauren hold Mangletooth in a cage at Camp Taurajo. He bears a bitter grudge against his own kind, saying his tribe betrayed him and cast him out.

Without freedom or his people's magic, he bargains with you for blood shards. Their power lets him reach Agamaggan's magic despite his captivity, then channel it to Horde champions. He takes pleasure in turning that power against the quilboar who rejected him.

sections.title: Razorfen's Sacred Roots
sections.body:
Mangletooth speaks with reverence of Razorfen, the quilboar's holiest sanctuary to the south. The tribes say the vast briars of Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs grew from Agamaggan's colossal skeleton and tusks.

They believe Razorfen Downs lies within the demigod's gaping maw. It is a holy threshold that devours and crushes any who enter without the Boar God's favor.

aliases: where do blood shards come from
faq.answer: Blood shards are red stones formed when Agamaggan's blood soaked into the earth during the War of the Ancients. They hold remnants of divine quilboar magic and may be found in mineral veins or carried by quilboar as totems.

faq.q: Why is Mangletooth willing to help the Horde?
faq.answer: Mangletooth is captive at Camp Taurajo, and says his own people turned their backs on him. Bitter over his exile and cut off from his people's sacred power, he offers to empower Horde champions against the quilboar who spurned him.

aliases: what do i get for blood shards
faq.answer: Mangletooth trades blood shards for temporary primal boons in Agamaggan's honor. They can enhance agility, strength, intellect, spirit, armor, and swift movement across the Barrens.

faq.q: Where is Razorfen, and what is its significance?
faq.answer: Razorfen lies in the southernmost Barrens. The quilboar revere it as their holiest site, believing its towering briars grew from Agamaggan's fallen body and Razorfen Downs is the demigod's colossal maw.

Agamaggan was an Ancient Guardian, a titanic boar god who died fighting the Burning Legion ten thousand years ago. His spilled blood raised the Barrens' massive razor-sharp brambles and gave the quilboar their birth and mystical strength.

faq.q: Can miners find blood shards in the Barrens?
faq.answer: Yes. Agamaggan's blood infused the Barrens' rocks and minerals, so miners sometimes find blood shards alongside ordinary tin and copper ore.

angles.text: Across the Barrens, miners can find blood shards embedded alongside tin and copper ore. They draw the crystallized blood of an Ancient Guardian from the veins.
As a tauren, you see the quilboar as aggressive rivals over the plains' dwindling water and game. Still, Agamaggan's sacrifice in the ancient war commands your spiritual respect.
To secure Camp Taurajo, the Horde must suppress the aggressive Bristleback and Razorfen tribes. A caged quilboar's spite can turn their demigod's strength against them.
As a shaman, you know blood shards hold raw, primordial earth and spirit magic. They speak to Kalimdor's deep shaping by titan-forged and primal spirits.
